subject: Post-call recap & benchmarks — latency/throughput follow-up (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood discovery — latency & throughput

John — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps:

- What we heard: Acme is evaluating inference options for your real-time assistant (avg. prompt 250 tokens, peaks up to 2k tokens) and needs 99th percentile latency under 350ms for short prompts and predictable tail behavior for longer contexts. You also called out sustained concurrency targets of ~400–600 concurrent requests.
- Immediate asks: a) representative latency/throughput numbers for the Llama 2 70B-like variant we demoed, b) guidance on batching and KV cache settings for your multi-session flows, c) a bridge path if you need private deployment.

Attached: a short benchmark packet (acme_latency_benchmarks_20260602.pdf) with our lab measurements and the KV cache notes Dylan promised to share. Key highlights from the packet:
- 256-token stable throughput: 450 reqs/s at p95 ~45ms when using continuous batching + async RPC (single dedicated 8xA100 pool).
- 2k-token tail (p99): ~320–420ms depending on batching window and quantization profile; we included a small table of kernel/sequence tradeoffs.
- Guidance: for your 400–600 concurrent target we recommend dedicated pooling + 20–40ms batching window and prefix KV caching for session-resumed calls.

Next steps suggested:
1) Dylan to share the raw runbook + bench notes (attached).
2) If these numbers look in range, propose a short POC (2-week smoke test) on a dedicated pool.
3) If legal/security is a blocker, we can scope a Private deployment plan.

Would love confirmation on whether the POC is still the right next step and who from Acme should own it.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0147

Attachment: acme_latency_benchmarks_20260602.pdf (15 pages)
Attachment: redwood_kvcache_notes.txt
From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-01T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood discovery — latency & throughput

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the packet. A couple of quick clarifying questions before we sync on a POC:

- For the 2k-token runs, were those cold-starts or with warmed KV cache? We expect a lot of resumed sessions.
- Can you share p99 tail stats for the exact config: quantized INT8, 8xA100, batching window 30ms, and 512 token context? We need that for our SRE review.
- Also: curious about the memory footprint you observed with the INT8 profile (we are tight on GPU memory in our initial plan).

If you can drop those numbers here that would be great — we might be able to fast-track the POC if numbers look favorable.

—John
John Doe
Principal Product Manager | Acme Corp
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-02T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood discovery — latency & throughput

Thanks for the follow-ups, John — quick answers + attached raw bench CSVs.

- 2k-token runs in the packet: mix of warmed KV cache (80% warmed, sessions with prefix cached). Cold-start p99 for 2k on the INT8 profile was ~540ms; warmed p99 fell to ~360ms.
- For the exact config you asked (INT8, 8xA100, batching window 30ms, 512 context): measured p99 = 185ms, p95 = 110ms, throughput ~320 reqs/s under steady-state parallelism. Numbers are from a run with our continuous batching enabled and async RPCs to maximize concurrency.
- Memory footprint (INT8 profile): model resident memory ~95 GB GPU (with our quantization packing), plus ~2–4 GB per concurrent KV cache shard depending on session size. If you're planning multi-tenant consolidation, we can show a slice with cuBLAS/cuDNN kernel selection differences.

Attached: acme_raw_benchmarks_20260602.csv, int8_memory_profile.png

If helpful I can schedule a short technical walk-through (20–30m) to go through the bench methodology—happy to do that with your SRE/ML infra folks.

—Dylan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
